sections.overview: The ginger carpetshark is a rarely recorded member of the Australian collar carpetsharks, known from a short stretch of Western Australia.
sections.identification: Its pale brown body bears a few relatively large, diffuse rusty spots and a faint collar-shaped mark behind the gills. The largest documented specimen was 78 cm long.
sections.habitat: It is recorded off southwestern Western Australia, from Fremantle to Cape Leeuwin. The three known specimens came from the upper continental slope at about 204–245 m.
sections.diet: Its diet has not been established; the available species accounts describe its biology as unknown.
sections.behavior: Species-specific behavior has not been documented in the sources consulted.
sections.reproduction: The FAO account classifies it as egg-laying, but the known specimens do not reveal its reproductive cycle.
sections.ecology: It is a deep-water relative of the varied carpetshark, P. variolatum, which is more broadly recorded in southern Australian coastal waters. Unlike that nearshore species, P. sparsimaculatum is known only from the upper slope off southwestern Australia.
sections.conservation: Its IUCN status is Data Deficient: the small number of records and lack of population data prevent a reliable risk estimate.
